heading: Friday, October 30, 2026
topLine: A trojanized build of the official Claude Code extension sat on Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours, planting an SSH backdoor on up to 5,000 developer machines.

items.headline: Backdoored Claude Code extension served through Cursor's marketplace to up to 5,000 users
items.summary: Version 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension, published under Anthropic's real extension ID, was live on Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours on Oct 29. It installed an attacker's SSH key, opened a reverse tunnel and set up persistence. Cursor says the build was not made by Anthropic and has rebuilt its marketplace and rotated keys. The clean 2.1.314 is out, the VS Code Marketplace and npm builds are reported clean, and researchers warn that uninstalling the extension is not enough if 2.1.313 was installed.

items.headline: Hugging Face launches Project ProtoStar to make publicly funded science AI-ready
items.summary: Hugging Face, CMU, Purdue, Georgia Tech, ASU, GWU and the Astera Institute are pushing for publicly funded datasets, models and code to be released in machine-actionable formats. The project runs open challenges, starting with a CMU climate-risk forecasting challenge for 210 US cities on Nov 2–13. Hugging Face says new science-dataset uploads in 2026 so far are more than triple the same period in 2025.

items.headline: OpenMausBot, an open-source group chat of AI agent bots, climbs GitHub trending
items.summary: Milind Soni's Apache-2.0 project is pitched as an open alternative to Grok Bot. Each bot in the chat app is a real agent driven through the Claude or Codex CLIs, with its own personality, model, cloud computer and connected apps. GitHub trending shows about 8.2k stars, 899 of them gained today.

items.headline: tinyworldformer runs a world model and its player on a $7 Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
items.summary: Two tiny networks run together on the microcontroller: an int8 world model of 26k–131k parameters that 'dreams' each frame of Breakout, Pong, Flappy Bird, Doom-lite or Pac-Man, and a 9k–16k-parameter actor that plays the game. It is a hobby project, not research, but it drew 261 points on HN.

image.alt: Breakout frames generated by the tiny world model

items.headline: AWS's EasyProver nearly saturates PutnamBench in Lean with an off-the-shelf Claude model
items.summary: A team from Amazon Web Services and Case Western built a proving harness around Anthropic's Fable-5 with no fine-tuning. The authors report it proved 669 of 672 PutnamBench problems and all six IMO 2026 formalizations, and resolved all 189 VERINA tasks. On a new Rust-to-Lean code-verification benchmark (Aegis) it proves only 52.7%, a sign that real-world code verification is now the harder target. These are the authors' own results; no open problems are claimed.

items.headline: OpenFrontiers: AI agents rarely rediscover 2026 math results without looking them up
items.summary: The authors collect 12,151 open research problems, mostly in mathematics, and build a 200-problem Lean benchmark: 110 problems solved by humans in 2026 and 90 still open. Seven LLM agents solved at most 7 of 40 resolved problems closed-book, and most of their live-web successes came from retrieving published solutions. That is a useful reality check on claims that AI is solving open problems.

items.headline: NVIDIA publishes the technical report for Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning
items.summary: The report covers NVIDIA's open hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts models: Super (about 120B total, 12B active, multimodal) and Lightning (about 30B total, 3B active). It details distillation, native speculative decoding and NVFP4 quantization. NVIDIA reports that Super scores 51.8% on SWE-bench Pro, ahead of Nemotron 3 Ultra with about 4.6× fewer active parameters, and reaches up to 4,856 output tokens/s per GPU on GB200.

items.headline: Intrinsic Distribution Matching: sharper two-step image generation without a helper network
items.summary: Today's most-upvoted Hugging Face paper, from Inclusion AI, Westlake, Tsinghua and others. It distills text-to-image models into one or two generation steps by reusing the generator's own features instead of training a separate helper network. The authors report better rendering of long text in images on Z-Image-Turbo and Qwen-Image at the same speed.

items.headline: UK competition regulator opens an abuse-of-dominance probe into Meta's terms for using publisher content in AI
items.summary: The CMA will examine whether Meta's new commercial terms let it take publishers' and businesses' content for its own products, AI features included, without a real opt-out. The investigation runs under Chapter II of the Competition Act. Meta has already pushed the rollout of the terms back from Oct 30 and says there are 'no grounds' for the probe.

items.headline: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings agrees to buy ADT for $15.3B to rebuild it around AI
items.summary: Thrive Capital's holding company, which OpenAI invests in and supplies with models and forward-deployed engineers, will pay $10 a share (about $7.6B in equity) for the home-security company. It is the largest deal yet in the 'buy a legacy business and retrofit it with AI' playbook, though no specific AI products have been announced.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs: workers displaced from AI-exposed jobs take longer to land new ones
items.summary: Goldman estimates that people laid off from AI-exposed roles since 2025 took about a month longer to find work than other displaced workers. They were also about 10 points more likely to still be unemployed a year later, and workers 35 and older fared worst. Goldman measured AI exposure by occupation and industry adoption rather than confirmed AI layoffs, and says the scarring matches past technology shocks.

items.headline: House progressives introduce a nonbinding resolution against bailing out AI companies
items.summary: Reps. Greg Casar and Maxine Waters' resolution says insolvent AI firms should go through ordinary bankruptcy rather than receive emergency loans, capital injections or debt guarantees. It also calls for clawbacks from executives and for aid to displaced workers. It has no legal force, but it topped HN's policy discussion with 411 points.
